descriptionHint: Find two distinct indices whose values add up to a target sum.
referenceApproach: Use a hash map to store each number and its index. As you iterate through the array, check if target minus current element exists in the map. If found, return the pair of indices; otherwise insert the current element into the map.

descriptionHint: Determine if any value appears at least twice in an integer array.
referenceApproach: Iterate through elements adding each to a hash set. If an element is already present in the set, return true. If iteration completes without finding duplicates, return false.

descriptionHint: Determine if string t is an anagram of string s.
referenceApproach: Check if lengths match. Use a fixed-size frequency array of size 26 (or hash map) to count character occurrences: increment for characters in s and decrement for characters in t. All counts must be zero.

descriptionHint: Group an array of strings into sublists of anagrams.
referenceApproach: Map character count tuples (or sorted string representations) as keys in a hash map. Collect strings sharing identical keys into lists in the map values.
optimalComplexity: O(n * k) time, O(n * k) space

descriptionHint: Return the k most frequent elements from an integer array.
referenceApproach: Count frequencies using a hash map. Group numbers by frequency into an array of buckets (indices represent frequency), then traverse buckets from right to left to collect the top k elements.

sources.title: Top K Frequent Elements in Array

descriptionHint: Compute output array where output[i] equals the product of all elements except nums[i] without division.
referenceApproach: Construct prefixes in the result array in a forward pass. In a backward pass, maintain a running suffix product and multiply with existing prefix values.

descriptionHint: Find length of the longest consecutive elements sequence in an unsorted array.
referenceApproach: Insert all numbers into a hash set. For each number num, only start counting if (num - 1) is not in the set (identifying sequence start). Increment counter as long as (num + 1) exists in the set.

descriptionHint: Determine if a phrase is a palindrome after converting to lowercase and stripping non-alphanumeric chars.
referenceApproach: Maintain two pointers at left and right extremes. Skip non-alphanumeric characters. Compare characters case-insensitively; if any mismatch occurs return false.

canonicalTitle: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
descriptionHint: Find two numbers in 1-indexed sorted array that add to target.
referenceApproach: Use two pointers starting at opposite ends. Sum the values: if sum == target, return indices. If sum < target, advance left pointer. If sum > target, decrement right pointer.

descriptionHint: Find all unique triplets in array that sum to zero.
referenceApproach: Sort the array. Iterate with index i from 0 to n - 3, skipping duplicates. For each i, run a two-pointer squeeze on the remaining range (i + 1 to n - 1) targeting -nums[i]. Skip duplicates after finding matches.

descriptionHint: Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the maximum water.
referenceApproach: Place left and right pointers at both ends. Compute area = min(height[left], height[right]) * (right - left). Move the pointer pointing to the shorter vertical bar inward, since only a taller bar can compensate for the decreased width.

descriptionHint: Compute how much water an elevation map can trap after raining.
referenceApproach: Two pointer approach: initialize left = 0, right = n - 1, left_max = 0, right_max = 0. While left < right, if height[left] < height[right], update left_max and add max(0, left_max - height[left]) to answer, left++. Else update right_max, add trapped water, right--. Alternative: monotonic decreasing stack of indices.
optimalComplexity: O(n) time, O(1) space (two pointers) or O(n) space (monotonic stack)

canonicalTitle: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
descriptionHint: Maximize single buy-then-sell profit given daily stock prices.
referenceApproach: Iterate through prices tracking the minimum price seen so far. At each day, calculate current profit = price - min_price, updating the max_profit if greater.

sources.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

descriptionHint: Find length of longest contiguous substring without recurring characters.
referenceApproach: Sliding window with hash map storing last observed index of each character. Expand right pointer; if char already seen inside current window, jump left pointer to last_index + 1. Update max length.

descriptionHint: Find length of longest substring with same letter allowing at most k character replacements.
referenceApproach: Sliding window tracking character frequencies and max_frequency in the window. If (window_length - max_frequency) > k, shift left pointer forward by 1, decrementing its frequency.

descriptionHint: Find minimum contiguous substring of s containing all characters of string t.
referenceApproach: Frequency map of target string t. Expand right pointer; when character matches requirement, increase count of matched unique chars. When all matched, contract left pointer while keeping window valid, recording shortest window.
optimalComplexity: O(n + m) time, O(n + m) space

descriptionHint: Find maximum value in every sliding window of size k.
referenceApproach: Maintain a monotonic decreasing deque storing indices. For each element at index i: remove indices outside the window (i - k); pop smaller elements from the back; push i; append front of deque to output once i >= k - 1.

sources.title: Maximum of Subarrays of Size K

descriptionHint: Determine if brackets string containing '()[]{}' is valid.
referenceApproach: Use a stack. Push expected closing brackets when an opening bracket is encountered. When a closing bracket appears, pop the stack and check for exact match. Return true if stack is empty at end.

descriptionHint: Find number of days to wait until a warmer temperature occurs.
referenceApproach: Monotonic decreasing stack storing indices. Iterate through temperatures: while current temp is greater than temp at stack top index, pop and calculate wait days = current_index - popped_index.

descriptionHint: Find the next greater element for each value in a subset array.
referenceApproach: Traverse the full array with a monotonic decreasing stack. Pop elements when a larger element appears, recording the next greater relationship in a hash map.

descriptionHint: Find the area of the largest rectangle in a histogram.
referenceApproach: Monotonic increasing stack storing pairs of (start_index, height). When a bar shorter than stack top is encountered, pop and compute area = height * (current_index - start_index). Extend start_index backward for new bar.

descriptionHint: Find index of target in sorted array in logarithmic time.
referenceApproach: Initialize left = 0, right = n - 1. While left <= right, compute mid = left + (right - left)/2. If nums[mid] == target return mid; if nums[mid] < target set left = mid + 1; else right = mid - 1.

descriptionHint: Find index of target in rotated sorted array of unique elements.
referenceApproach: Modified binary search: determine which half is sorted. If nums[left] <= nums[mid], left half is sorted: check if target lies within nums[left] and nums[mid]. Otherwise right half is sorted: check if target lies within nums[mid] and nums[right].

canonicalTitle: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
descriptionHint: Find minimum element in rotated sorted array of unique elements.
referenceApproach: Binary search: if nums[mid] > nums[right], the inflection point and minimum must be in the right half (left = mid + 1). Otherwise, right = mid.

sources.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

descriptionHint: Find minimum integer eating speed k to eat all bananas within h hours.
referenceApproach: Binary search on speed k from 1 to max(piles). For each candidate speed k, calculate total hours required: sum of ceil(pile / k). If total hours <= h, valid speed (search left: right = mid); otherwise search right (left = mid + 1).

descriptionHint: Reverse a singly linked list iteratively in-place.
referenceApproach: Use 3 pointers: prev (null), curr (head), next. In a loop, save curr.next, redirect curr.next = prev, advance prev = curr, advance curr = next. Return prev as new head.

descriptionHint: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list.
referenceApproach: Use a dummy head node and a current pointer. While both lists have elements, append the node with the smaller value to current.next and advance that list. Append remaining non-empty tail at end.

descriptionHint: Determine if a linked list contains a cycle.
referenceApproach: Floyd's Tortoise and Hare: slow pointer moves 1 step, fast pointer moves 2 steps. If fast meets slow, a cycle exists. If fast or fast.next reaches null, no cycle exists.

descriptionHint: Find contiguous subarray with the largest sum (Kadane's algorithm).
referenceApproach: Kadane's algorithm: maintain current_sum and max_sum. For each element num, current_sum = max(num, current_sum + num). Update max_sum = max(max_sum, current_sum).

descriptionHint: Count distinct ways to climb n steps taking 1 or 2 steps at a time.
referenceApproach: Fibonacci relation: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). Base cases ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2. Track previous two variables iteratively in O(1) space.

sources.title: Count Ways to Reach the Nth Stair

descriptionHint: Determine max money robbed from houses along a street without robbing adjacent houses.
referenceApproach: Dynamic programming: at each house i, choice is rob current (nums[i] + rob_prev2) or skip (rob_prev1). dp[i] = max(nums[i] + dp[i-2], dp[i-1]). Update two state variables in O(1) memory.

descriptionHint: Find fewest number of coins needed to make up a given amount.
referenceApproach: Bottom-up 1D DP array of size amount + 1 initialized to amount + 1. dp[0] = 0. For i from 1 to amount, for each coin c: if i >= c, dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - c]). Return dp[amount] if != amount + 1 else -1.

descriptionHint: Find length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in an array.
referenceApproach: Patience sorting with binary search: maintain an array 'tails' storing smallest tail of all increasing subsequences of various lengths. For each x in nums, binary search x in tails; replace if found or append if greater than all. Length of tails is answer.
optimalComplexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

descriptionHint: Find length of the longest common subsequence between two strings.
referenceApproach: 2D DP table where dp[i][j] represents LCS length of text1[0..i] and text2[0..j]. If text1[i] == text2[j], dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise, dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
optimalComplexity: O(n * m) time, O(min(n, m)) space

descriptionHint: Count number of distinct 4-directionally connected islands of '1's in a grid.
referenceApproach: Traverse grid cell by cell. When an unvisited '1' is found, increment island count and initiate BFS or DFS to sink all connected '1's by marking them '0'.
optimalComplexity: O(rows * cols) time, O(rows * cols) space

descriptionHint: Determine if you can finish all courses given prerequisite DAG constraints.
referenceApproach: Topological sort via Kahn's algorithm: compute indegree of all vertices. Push all 0-indegree courses into queue. Pop course, decrement indegrees of neighbors, enqueue if 0. Count processed courses; if equals numCourses, return true, else cycle exists.
optimalComplexity: O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space

descriptionHint: Merge all overlapping intervals and return non-overlapping intervals covering all input.
referenceApproach: Sort intervals by start time. Iterate through intervals: if current interval overlaps with the previous (start <= prev.end), merge them by updating prev.end = max(prev.end, current.end). Otherwise append current interval.
optimalComplexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

descriptionHint: Invert a binary tree by swapping left and right subtrees recursively.
referenceApproach: Recursively invert the left and right subtrees of each node and swap their pointers, returning the root.

descriptionHint: Find the maximum number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf.
referenceApproach: Use depth-first search: return 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)). Can also be solved iteratively via level-order BFS.

descriptionHint: Check if two binary trees are structurally identical with equal values.
referenceApproach: Recursively compare roots: if both null, true; if one null or values differ, false; otherwise recurse on left and right children.

descriptionHint: Determine if a binary tree contains another tree as a subtree.
referenceApproach: Traverse tree with DFS. At each node, check if the subtree rooted there is identical to subRoot using Same Tree helper.

canonicalTitle: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
descriptionHint: Find the lowest shared ancestor node of two given nodes p and q in a BST.
referenceApproach: Leverage BST ordering: if both values are greater than root, search right; if both smaller, search left; the split point is the LCA.

sources.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree

descriptionHint: Return the level-by-level node values from left to right.
referenceApproach: Use a queue for BFS. For each level, record queue size and iterate through all current level nodes, adding children to queue.

descriptionHint: Determine if a binary tree is a valid Binary Search Tree with strictly ordered keys.
referenceApproach: Recursively validate that each node value lies strictly between allowed lower and upper bounds (minVal, maxVal).

canonicalTitle: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
descriptionHint: Find the kth smallest value (1-indexed) in a BST.
referenceApproach: In-order traversal visits BST nodes in monotonically ascending order. Stop and return when the kth node is reached.

sources.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST

canonicalTitle: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
descriptionHint: Reconstruct a binary tree given preorder and inorder traversal arrays.
referenceApproach: First element of preorder is root. Locate root in inorder using hash map to partition left and right subtrees, then recurse.

sources.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal

descriptionHint: Find the maximum sequence sum along any non-empty path through nodes in a binary tree.
referenceApproach: Post-order DFS: for each node, compute max single-branch gain (ignoring negatives). Update global max path with node + leftGain + rightGain.

descriptionHint: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree into a string and deserialize it back.
referenceApproach: Pre-order DFS serialization with delimiter and '#' for null nodes. Deserialization consumes tokens recursively reconstructing tree.

descriptionHint: Implement a trie supporting insert, search, and startsWith operations.
referenceApproach: Each TrieNode contains an array/map of 26 children and an isEndOfWord boolean flag. Traverse node by node for operations.
optimalComplexity: O(L) time per operation, O(total keys * L) space

canonicalTitle: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
descriptionHint: Design a data structure supporting exact word addition and dot wildcard character matching.
referenceApproach: Store words in a Trie. For search, standard lookup for characters and recursive DFS across all children for wildcard '.'.
optimalComplexity: O(L) insert, O(26^d * L) search with wildcards

sources.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

descriptionHint: Find all words from a dictionary present in a 2D board of characters.
referenceApproach: Build a Trie from the word dictionary. Run DFS from each cell in the board, pruning search immediately when Trie path terminates.
optimalComplexity: O(M * N * 4^L) time, O(total words * L) space

descriptionHint: Merge k sorted linked lists and return it as one sorted list.
referenceApproach: Maintain a min-heap containing head node of each list. Continuously pop minimum, append to result, and push next node.
optimalComplexity: O(N log k) time, O(k) space

descriptionHint: Design a data structure that dynamically supports adding numbers and retrieving the current median.
referenceApproach: Maintain two heaps: max-heap for lower half and min-heap for upper half. Keep sizes balanced within difference of 1.
optimalComplexity: O(log n) addNum, O(1) findMedian, O(n) space

descriptionHint: Find all unique combinations of candidate numbers that sum to a given target, allowing reuse.
referenceApproach: Backtracking: sort candidates. At each step, choose to include candidate (stay at same index) or skip to next index. Prune when sum exceeds target.

descriptionHint: Check if a given word exists in a 2D grid of letters using sequentially adjacent cells.
referenceApproach: Standard backtracking DFS from each matching starting cell. Mark visited cells in-place with a sentinel character and restore on backtrack.
optimalComplexity: O(M * N * 3^L) time, O(L) recursion stack

canonicalTitle: Remove Nth Node From End of List
descriptionHint: Remove the nth node from the end of a singly linked list in a single pass.
referenceApproach: Two pointers with dummy head: advance fast pointer n + 1 steps ahead. Move both fast and slow together until fast reaches null, then delete slow.next.

sources.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List

descriptionHint: Reorder a linked list to L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> L2 -> Ln-2 in-place.
referenceApproach: Find midpoint using slow/fast pointers. Reverse second half in-place. Interweave the two halves using two pointers.

descriptionHint: Create a deep copy of a connected undirected graph.
referenceApproach: Use a hash map mapping original nodes to cloned copies. Traverse using BFS or DFS, cloning edges as neighbor relationships are discovered.

descriptionHint: Find all grid coordinates from which water can flow to both Pacific and Atlantic oceans.
referenceApproach: Reverse flow: run multi-source BFS/DFS inward from Pacific borders and Atlantic borders uphill (height >= current). Find intersection of visited sets.
optimalComplexity: O(M * N) time, O(M * N) space

descriptionHint: Return the ordering of courses you should take to finish all courses given prerequisite edges.
referenceApproach: Kahn's algorithm: compute in-degrees. Initialize queue with 0 in-degree nodes. Append to ordering and decrement neighbors' in-degrees. Check if all courses included.
optimalComplexity: O(V + E) time, O(V + E) space

descriptionHint: Determine if given undirected edges form a single valid tree.
referenceApproach: A valid tree must have exactly n - 1 edges and no cycles (fully connected). Use Disjoint Set (Union-Find) or BFS.

canonicalTitle: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
descriptionHint: Count the number of disconnected components in an undirected graph.
referenceApproach: Union-Find with path compression. Start with n components and decrement count whenever two distinct root parents are successfully merged.
optimalComplexity: O(V + E * alpha(V)) time, O(V) space

sources.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph

descriptionHint: Derive the unique alphabetical ordering of characters from a sorted list of alien words.
referenceApproach: Compare adjacent words to extract directed character precedence edges. Build DAG and apply Kahn's topological sort or cycle detection DFS.
optimalComplexity: O(C) time where C is total length of all words, O(U + min(U^2, N)) space

descriptionHint: Houses are arranged in a circle. Maximize robbery loot without alerting adjacent security systems.
referenceApproach: Since first and last houses are adjacent, solve two standard 1D linear subproblems: houses[0...n-2] and houses[1...n-1]. Return max of both.

descriptionHint: Count the number of ways to decode a numeric string into letters (1->A, 26->Z).
referenceApproach: 1D DP: dp[i] = dp[i-1] (if s[i-1] != '0') + dp[i-2] (if substring s[i-2...i-1] is between 10 and 26). Maintain previous two values.

descriptionHint: Calculate distinct paths from top-left to bottom-right in an m x n grid moving only down and right.
referenceApproach: 2D DP grid: dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]. Optimize space to a single 1D array of width n.

descriptionHint: Determine if you are able to reach the last index starting from index 0 with max jump lengths.
referenceApproach: Greedy approach: iterate from left to right tracking max reachable index. If current index exceeds max reachable, return false; if max >= last, return true.

descriptionHint: Determine if string s can be segmented into space-separated dictionary words.
referenceApproach: 1D boolean DP: dp[i] is true if s[0...i] can be segmented. For each i, check all j < i where dp[j] is true and s[j...i] exists in dictionary set.

descriptionHint: Count the number of possible ordered permutations of numbers adding up to target sum.
referenceApproach: Unbounded knapsack permutation DP: dp[i] = sum(dp[i - num]) for all num in nums where i >= num. Base case dp[0] = 1.

descriptionHint: Find a contiguous non-empty subarray that has the largest product.
referenceApproach: Kadane's variant: track both maxProduct and minProduct ending at current index since multiplying by a negative flips minimum to maximum.

descriptionHint: Insert a new interval into a sorted non-overlapping list and merge if necessary.
referenceApproach: Add all intervals ending before newInterval starts. Merge all overlapping intervals into newInterval by extending bounds. Add remaining intervals.

descriptionHint: Find minimum number of intervals to remove to make the rest non-overlapping.
referenceApproach: Greedy interval scheduling: sort by end time. Keep the interval that finishes earliest to maximize room for subsequent intervals.
optimalComplexity: O(n log n) time, O(1) space

descriptionHint: Determine if a person could attend all scheduled meetings without conflict.
referenceApproach: Sort intervals by start time. Check if any meeting starts before the previous meeting ends (intervals[i].start < intervals[i-1].end).
optimalComplexity: O(n log n) time, O(1) space

descriptionHint: Find the minimum number of conference rooms required for all meetings.
referenceApproach: Chronological line sweep: separate start times and end times into two sorted arrays. Increment active rooms on start and decrement on end.
optimalComplexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

descriptionHint: Rotate an n x n 2D matrix 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
referenceApproach: Transpose matrix across main diagonal (swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i]), then reverse each individual row horizontally.

descriptionHint: Return all elements of an m x n matrix in clockwise spiral order.
referenceApproach: Maintain 4 boundary pointers: top, bottom, left, right. Traverse top row, right column, bottom row, left column, shrinking boundaries after each pass.
optimalComplexity: O(m * n) time, O(1) extra space

descriptionHint: If an element in an m x n matrix is 0, set its entire row and column to 0 in-place.
referenceApproach: Use first row and first column as zero markers. Use separate boolean variables for whether row 0 and column 0 themselves need to be zeroed.

descriptionHint: Calculate Hamming weight: number of set bits in an unsigned integer.
referenceApproach: Brian Kernighan's algorithm: repeatedly clear least significant set bit using n = n & (n - 1) until n becomes 0.
optimalComplexity: O(k) time where k is number of set bits, O(1) space

descriptionHint: For every number 0 <= i <= n, count the number of 1s in its binary representation in O(n).
referenceApproach: DP with bit shift: dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1). Each number's bit count is known from its right-shifted prefix plus parity bit.

descriptionHint: Reverse the 32 bits of a given unsigned integer.
referenceApproach: Iterate 32 times: shift result left by 1, bitwise OR with (n & 1), then right shift n by 1.

descriptionHint: Find the only missing integer in the range [0, n] from an array of n numbers.
referenceApproach: XOR all indices 0..n with all array values. Since x ^ x = 0, duplicates cancel out leaving the missing number.

descriptionHint: Calculate the sum of two integers without using the operators + and -.
referenceApproach: Bitwise addition: sum without carry is a ^ b. Carry is (a & b) << 1. Repeat until carry is zero.

descriptionHint: Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a list of strings cleanly.
referenceApproach: Length-prefix encoding: encode each string as '<length>#<string>'. Decoding reads length up to '#', extracts exactly that many characters, and repeats.
optimalComplexity: O(total characters) time, O(1) auxiliary space

descriptionHint: Return the longest contiguous palindromic substring in s.
referenceApproach: Expand around centers: iterate through each character (odd length center) and between characters (even length center), expanding outward while characters match.

descriptionHint: Count the total number of contiguous palindromic substrings in string s.
referenceApproach: Expand around centers: for each of the 2n - 1 potential centers, expand outward counting every valid symmetric expansion.

descriptionHint: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.
referenceApproach: Maintain two stacks or store pairs (val, currentMin). On push, currentMin is min(val, minStack.peek()).
optimalComplexity: O(1) time per operation, O(n) space

descriptionHint: Evaluate arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation using standard operators.
referenceApproach: Use stack: push operands. When operator is encountered, pop top two operands, evaluate operator, and push result back.

descriptionHint: Generate all combinations of n pairs of well-formed parentheses.
referenceApproach: Backtracking: add open paren if openCount < n; add close paren if closeCount < openCount. Terminate when length == 2*n.
optimalComplexity: O(4^n / sqrt(n)) Catalan number time and space

descriptionHint: Determine how many car fleets will arrive at the destination target position.
referenceApproach: Calculate time to target for each car. Sort by position descending. Use monotonic stack to identify cars that collide and merge fleets.
optimalComplexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

descriptionHint: Search target in an m x n sorted matrix where each row is sorted and first integer of each row > last of previous.
referenceApproach: Treat 2D matrix as a flat sorted 1D array of size m * n. Standard binary search with index mapping: row = mid / n, col = mid % n.

descriptionHint: Design a key-value store that supports retrieving values at specific historical timestamps.
referenceApproach: Map key to a list of pairs (timestamp, value). Since set timestamps are strictly increasing, use binary search to find floor timestamp.
optimalComplexity: O(1) set, O(log k) get, O(n) space

descriptionHint: Find the median of two sorted arrays of size m and n in O(log(min(m, n))) time.
referenceApproach: Binary search partition on the smaller array so that total elements in left partition equals right partition and maxLeft <= minRight.

descriptionHint: Add two numbers represented by linked lists in reverse order with digit nodes.
referenceApproach: Simulate digit addition with carry. Iterate through both lists until both are null and carry is 0, creating new nodes.
optimalComplexity: O(max(m, n)) time, O(max(m, n)) space

descriptionHint: Deep copy a linked list where each node has a next and a random pointer.
referenceApproach: Interweave copied nodes immediately after original nodes (A -> A' -> B -> B'). Copy random pointers: curr.next.random = curr.random.next. Unweave.

descriptionHint: Find the duplicate number in an array containing n + 1 integers in range [1, n] without modifying array.
referenceApproach: Floyd's cycle detection: treat array as linked list where index i points to nums[i]. Find intersection using slow/fast, then find cycle start.

descriptionHint: Design a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with O(1) get and put operations.
referenceApproach: Combine a Hash Map with a Doubly Linked List. Map provides O(1) lookup to nodes; DLL provides O(1) node relocation and eviction.
optimalComplexity: O(1) time per get/put, O(capacity) space

descriptionHint: Find length of the longest path between any two nodes in a tree (path may or may not pass through root).
referenceApproach: Post-order DFS: for each node, compute max depth of left and right subtrees. Update global max diameter with leftDepth + rightDepth.

descriptionHint: Determine if binary tree is height-balanced (left and right heights differ by at most 1 at every node).
referenceApproach: Bottom-up DFS: return -1 if any subtree is unbalanced. Otherwise return 1 + max(leftHeight, rightHeight) to parent.

descriptionHint: Return values of the nodes visible when viewing binary tree from the right side.
referenceApproach: BFS level order traversal: the last element popped from each level queue is added to result list.

descriptionHint: Generate all possible subsets (the power set) of a unique integer array.
referenceApproach: Backtracking: at each index, recursively branch by including nums[i] in the current subset and excluding it.

descriptionHint: Return all possible permutations of an array of distinct integers.
referenceApproach: Backtracking: maintain boolean visited array or swap elements in place. At each depth, iterate through available candidates.

descriptionHint: Find minimum minutes until no fresh orange remains in grid, or -1 if impossible.
referenceApproach: Multi-source BFS: enqueue all initially rotten oranges. In each step, rot 4-directionally adjacent fresh oranges and decrement fresh count.
optimalComplexity: O(m * n) time, O(m * n) space

descriptionHint: Find minimum cost to reach the top of the floor starting at index 0 or 1.
referenceApproach: 1D DP: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). Maintain two variables for constant space.

descriptionHint: Find starting gas station index to travel clockwise around circuit once, or -1.
referenceApproach: Greedy: if totalGas < totalCost, impossible (-1). Otherwise, reset candidate start whenever cumulative tank dips below 0.

descriptionHint: Sort an array of 0s, 1s, and 2s in-place in a single pass (Dutch National Flag problem).
referenceApproach: Three pointers: low, mid, high. Swap 0s to low, 2s to high, and advance mid on 1s.

descriptionHint: Find element appearing more than n / 2 times in an array.
referenceApproach: Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm: maintain candidate and count. Increment count on match, decrement on mismatch; reset candidate when count == 0.

descriptionHint: Find next lexicographical permutation of numbers in-place.
referenceApproach: Scan from right to find pivot where nums[i] < nums[i+1]. Swap nums[i] with next larger element to its right. Reverse suffix from i+1 to end.

descriptionHint: Generate the first numRows of Pascal's triangle.
referenceApproach: Each row starts and ends with 1. Intermediate values are row[j] = prevRow[j-1] + prevRow[j].

canonicalTitle: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
descriptionHint: Find lowest common ancestor of two nodes p and q in any binary tree.
referenceApproach: Post-order DFS: if root is null, p, or q, return root. Recurse left and right. If both return non-null, root is LCA; otherwise return the non-null child.

sources.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree

canonicalTitle: Kth Largest Element in an Array
descriptionHint: Find the kth largest element in an unsorted array.
referenceApproach: Maintain a min-heap of size k. Push elements and pop when size > k; top of heap is kth largest. Alternatively, Quickselect in O(n) average time.
optimalComplexity: O(n log k) time, O(k) space

sources.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array

descriptionHint: Find k closest points to the origin (0, 0) on the X-Y plane.
referenceApproach: Maintain a max-heap of size k storing points sorted by distance x^2 + y^2. Pop farthest point whenever size exceeds k.
optimalComplexity: O(n log k) time, O(k) space

descriptionHint: Find minimum CPU intervals needed to execute all tasks with cooling period n.
referenceApproach: Max frequency formula: let maxFreq be frequency of most frequent task, and countMax be tasks with that frequency. Idle slots = (maxFreq - 1) * (n - (countMax - 1)). Answer is max(tasks.length, (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + countMax).

descriptionHint: Determine if a 9 x 9 Sudoku board is valid according to row, column, and sub-box rules.
referenceApproach: Use hash sets or bitmasks to track numbers seen in each of the 9 rows, 9 columns, and 9 3x3 sub-boxes.

descriptionHint: Return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1 as a contiguous substring.
referenceApproach: Fixed-size sliding window of length s1.length over s2. Maintain frequency count difference and count of matching character frequencies.

descriptionHint: Find all unique subsets of an integer array that may contain duplicates.
referenceApproach: Sort array. In backtracking DFS, skip duplicate sibling branches: if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1], continue.

descriptionHint: Find all unique combinations where numbers sum to target; each number used at most once.
referenceApproach: Sort candidates. When branching, advance index to i + 1 (single use) and skip adjacent duplicate elements at the same tree depth.

canonicalTitle: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
descriptionHint: Return all letter combinations that the number could represent from phone keypad.
referenceApproach: Map digits to keypad letters. Backtracking DFS explores all combinations by picking one letter per digit index.

descriptionHint: Capture all regions surrounded by 'X' by converting surrounded 'O's into 'X's.
referenceApproach: Boundary flood fill: start BFS/DFS from 'O's on matrix borders, marking them as uncapturable ('#'). Then flip remaining 'O's to 'X' and '#' back to 'O'.
optimalComplexity: O(m * n) time, O(m * n) space

descriptionHint: Determine if array can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum.
referenceApproach: 0/1 Knapsack DP: if total sum is odd, false. Target = sum / 2. dp[j] boolean indicates if sum j can be formed, iterating backwards to prevent reuse.

descriptionHint: Assign + or - to each integer to reach target sum.
referenceApproach: Transform to subset sum: P - N = target and P + N = sum => P = (target + sum) / 2. Solve 0/1 knapsack for sum P.

descriptionHint: Find minimum operations (insert, delete, replace) to convert word1 to word2.
referenceApproach: 2D DP: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if characters match, else 1 + min(insert: dp[i][j-1], delete: dp[i-1][j], replace: dp[i-1][j-1]).

descriptionHint: Find the element that appears once in an array where every other element appears twice.
referenceApproach: Bitwise XOR: XOR of a number with itself is 0, and 0 ^ x = x. XORing all elements leaves the unique single number.
